findings.evidence: Row claims version "2", version_status "published", status "active". SOURCE 1 (current captured protocol) is titled "WeirdML v3" and features "11 complex hand-made tasks"; it states "Previous versions: WeirdML v2 · WeirdML v1." The maintainer publishes a release identifier for this board and the current one is "3", not "2". A changed task set (11 vs 17), scoring rule and release version cannot silently keep the live v2 identity. Repair: repoint the row to the current published identity (version "3" with v3 scoring and 11 tasks), or freeze v2 with status "retained" and version_status "retained".
findings.repair: Update row to current v3 identity, or mark it a deliberately retained v2 record.

findings.evidence: Row status is "active". The protocol lists "WeirdML v2" under "Previous versions", i.e. the board was replaced by v3 going forward; that is the c2 definition of "retained". SOURCE 2's 2 changed avg_acc values come from the current (v3) served payload and evidence v3 being reported, not v2.
findings.repair: Set status to "retained" if the row stays the v2 record, or make it the v3 row with status "active".

findings.evidence: Row has superseded_by: null, but the protocol names the successor board: "WeirdML v3" is the current benchmark and "WeirdML v2" is a previous version. Per c2, null is a mismatch when the protocol names a successor.
findings.repair: Set superseded_by to the registry id of the WeirdML v3 board.

findings.evidence: Row metric: "Average Max Accuracy ... 5 iterations per run, averaged over all 17 tasks". The current protocol's official score is "80% normalized area under its line on a logarithmic token axis, plus 20% of its final value" over "11 tasks" with hinted/hintless twin weighting; nothing in the excerpt supports 17 tasks or max-accuracy-over-5-iterations scoring, and the task-set size contradicts it. Description's "fixed compute and time limits" also does not match the current token-window (500k-50M) framing.
findings.repair: Replace metric/description with the current v3 scoring rule and task count, or downgrade the row to a retained v2 record per f1.

uncertainties: Row and source hashes are owner-computed; I cannot recompute SHA-256 or re-run transport/qualification checks, which is a limitation of this review, not missing evidence.

The v2 board's own historical protocol text is not in the packet, so the historical accuracy of the v2 metric wording cannot be independently verified; the findings rest on the contradiction between the row's live/active claim and the current v3 protocol, which the excerpt settles.

unit "percent" and range [0,100] are consistent with the served avg_acc scale (162 values, 1.729411764705882 to 93.57264705882352) per c1, but that summary says nothing about metric meaning and does not cure f4.
